official.deadline_note: No separate scholarship deadline - SUTD states that application for the scholarships is made at the same time as application for admission to SUTD. The most recently published admissions window ran 2 January to 2 March 2026 for all other qualifications, and from the day of release of A-Level results to 19 March 2026 for the Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level qualification; the next cycle's dates had not been published as of 10 October 2026.
official.application_cycle: Annual, tied to the SUTD undergraduate admissions cycle (2026 window published; next-cycle dates not yet published)
official.status_note: The scholarship page carries no open/closed marker or deadline; SUTD evaluates admission and scholarship applications together and informs applicants of the specific scholarship awarded along with the admission offer. As of 10 October 2026 the next admissions window had not been announced, so the coming round is upcoming.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Scholarship covers the subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant) for the normal duration (up to four years) of the respective bachelor degree programmes at SUTD. For Scholarships awarded to Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students, tuition fees coverage will be capped at the fees payable by a Singapore Citizen.
official.funding_period: per academic year, for up to four years
benefits: Subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant) for the normal duration (up to four years) of the respective bachelor degree programme at SUTD
No bond is attached to the Scholarship
Coverage for Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students is capped at the fees payable by a Singapore Citizen
eligibility: Singapore Citizens applying for admission to SUTD's undergraduate degree programme
Outstanding Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications
Have a passion for technology and design
As a special concession, the Scholarship may also be awarded to Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students who have demonstrated exceptional and outstanding achievements
requirements: The recipient must take up the Tuition Grant Scheme (TGS) from the Singapore Government to enjoy subsidised fees
The recipient is required to achieve and maintain good academic standing; academic performance will be reviewed every term
Recipients are required to complete at least 20 hours of service to the University (e.g. student ambassador, publicity talks, receiving guests)
Recipients may not, without the approval of the University, hold concurrently any other scholarships or grants
Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents must fulfil the Mother Tongue Language (MTL) admission requirement
documents: Copy of the front and back of the NRIC (for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents) or the Passport particulars page (for International Students)
Academic Transcripts and Certificates at secondary/junior high and senior high school levels
Official English proficiency test result (IELTS, TOEFL, SAT, PTE Academic, ACT or C1 Advanced) where required - compulsory for qualifications where English is not the medium of instruction
Contact details of up to two referees, with school or other relevant testimonial(s)/recommendation letter(s) uploaded
Supporting documents for outstanding/relevant achievements listed (e.g. SGC), from within the last four years
Declaration of gross monthly household income and answers to the scholarship/financial-aid questions in the application
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded on the basis of competition among eligible applicants
SUTD reserves the right not to award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit
The decision of the selection committee is final; enquiries or disputes surrounding its decisions will not be entertained

Assessed holistically with the admission application: academic competency focused on Mathematics and the Sciences, qualities/traits, portfolio (co-curricular activities, notable accomplishments, leadership, teacher recommendations, personal insight questions), and an interview for selected candidates
coverage: Subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant for the normal duration (up to four years / 8 terms) of the respective SUTD bachelor degree programme
Coverage capped at the fees payable by a Singapore Citizen when awarded to a Singapore Permanent Resident or International Student
Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees, housing and all living expenses are not covered (CMF for AY2026: S$10 one-time enrolment fee plus S$165 per term for SC/SPR, inclusive of GST)
application_method: Indicate interest in applying for SUTD scholarships in the admission application - there is no separate scholarship form
Submit only one electronic application through the SUTD Admissions System (duplicate applications will not be processed)
Declare gross monthly household income and answer the scholarship/financial-aid questions in the application
Shortlisted applicants will be notified in due course; the award is announced together with the admission offer
official.application_route: Apply through the SUTD Admissions System for admission and indicate interest in SUTD scholarships within the same application; admission and scholarship are assessed together.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Singapore Citizens applying for admission to an SUTD undergraduate degree programme; as a special concession it may also be awarded to Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students who have demonstrated exceptional and outstanding achievements.
official.international_eligibility: Only by special concession: International Students may be awarded the Scholarship only if they have demonstrated exceptional and outstanding achievements, and their tuition coverage is capped at the fees payable by a Singapore Citizen.
official.duration: Normal duration of the respective SUTD bachelor degree programme, up to four years (8 terms)
official.description: The SUTD Undergraduate Merit Scholarship recognises outstanding students who demonstrate academic excellence and have a penchant for creating radical technology and innovative designs. It covers the subsidised tuition fees, after the Tuition Grant, for the normal duration (up to four years) of the respective SUTD bachelor degree programme, with no bond attached.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition scholarship for new undergraduate admission applicants
official.english_requirement: SUTD publishes no minimum score. Submission of IELTS, TOEFL (internet-based), SAT, PTE Academic, ACT or C1 Advanced scores is compulsory for applicants presenting qualifications where English is not the medium of instruction (including Indonesian Ijazah SMA, Indonesian Ujian Nasional, Myanmar Matriculation Examination, PRC Gao Kao/NCEE, UEC, STPM and the Vietnam National High School Graduation Examination); only scores obtained in the two years leading up to the application are considered. No English test is required of Singapore Citizens applying under local qualifications.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition waiver, not a living scholarship: it pays your subsidised SUTD tuition fee (after the Tuition Grant) for the normal four-year programme, worth S$13,500 per academic year at the Singapore-Citizen rate, but it leaves accommodation, Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees and day-to-day living costs entirely on you. There is no separate scholarship form and no scholarship deadline of its own - you are considered simply by ticking scholarship interest inside your SUTD admission application, and shortlisted candidates are told only when offers go out. In practice you compete for it against every other strong SUTD applicant in your qualification pool, and SUTD can decline to award it at all if nobody clears the merit bar. If you are a Singapore Citizen with top A-Level, polytechnic, NUS High or IB results who genuinely wants a design-and-technology degree, this belongs high on your list - but pair it with financial aid or the donor scholarships rather than expecting it to fund you outright.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore-Citizen high school leavers with standout A-Level, polytechnic, NUS High or IB results (and demonstrable technology-and-design interest) who are already set on SUTD and just need tuition taken care of.
application_readiness_checklist: Prepare the SUTD application (transcripts, NRIC copy, referee details) first - the scholarship is judged from that same file, so a thin admission application kills the scholarship too

Secure two referees early (a teacher from your school/polytechnic who has known you academically for at least half a year) and get their written consent before listing them, since testimonials must be uploaded
Line up supporting evidence (certificates, SGC records) for any achievement, leadership or research activity you list - claims from the last four years only
Draft strong answers to the personal insight questions; these are explicitly part of the holistic review and your only chance to show drive, curiosity and resilience beyond grades
Declare gross monthly household income accurately, because the same figure feeds the donor-scholarship and financial-aid assessment you are opting into
Note your Tuition Grant declaration in the application - the scholarship only works if the Tuition Grant is taken up
common_rejection_risks: Applying late or missing the admissions window entirely - with no separate deadline there is no fallback window for the scholarship
Weak profile outside grades: the review is holistic, so thin co-curricular, leadership or portfolio evidence sinks otherwise strong candidates
Referees who cannot speak to recent academic work, or missing testimonials where the application expects them
Competitive pools: SUTD explicitly reserves the right not to award if no candidate is of sufficient merit, so a strong file is necessary but not sufficient
Listing achievements without uploaded proof, or claiming experiences older than four years
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition: host or own accommodation (housing fees are charged separately), Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees (S$10 one-time enrolment fee plus S$165 per term for SC/SPR, inclusive of GST), meals, transport, laptop and personal expenses, plus any fees for terms beyond the normal 8-term candidature.
document_audit: NRIC scans must show both front and back clearly - incomplete uploads stall verification
Transcripts and certificates are needed at both secondary/junior high AND senior high levels; polytechnic applicants often forget the secondary-level documents

English test reports must be from the two years before application and sent with the correct SUTD institution codes (7216 for TOEFL, 6532 for SAT, 7989 for ACT) if your qualification is not taught in English
Only one application is processed - resubmitting a duplicate form to 'fix' a mistake can void both
Referee consent is required before listing them; testimonials/recommendation letters are uploads, not auto-generated requests
alerts: The scholarship has no bond, but the Tuition Grant it depends on does not follow the same rule for non-citizens: PRs who take the Tier B grant and international students who take the Tier C grant must work for a Singapore entity for three years after graduation
You may not hold this scholarship concurrently with any other scholarship or grant without University approval - check before accepting a donor award on top
Because awards are donor-supported, recipients may be asked to write appreciation notes and attend university or donor events

Coverage for a PR or international awardee is capped at the Singapore-Citizen fee, so PRs (subsidised fee S$19,350/yr from AY2026) or international students (S$30,200+/yr) still face a large residual fee
SUTD reviews academic standing every term and can withdraw the award, or require repayment if you leave early, so treat renewal as performance-based
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online SUTD Admissions System application with the scholarship box ticked, assessed jointly with admission; shortlisted candidates are contacted and the award is communicated together with the admission offer.
